newsitem.title: FRANCE: Saudi Arabia, France urge return to calm in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia, France urge return to calm in Iraq.

text.p: Saudi Arabia and France on Wednesday urged a return to calm in Iraq, where Washington and Baghdad are in a military standoff.

"We want to see wisdom and reason prevail, calm to be restored, and the integrity of Iraq to be protected," Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Saud al-Faisal said after talks with President Jacques Chirac.
France and Saudi Arabia were part of the U.S.-led coalition that drove Iraq out of Kuwait in the 1991 Gulf War but have distanced themselves from Washington in the latest crisis.
On Tuesday, Saud and French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette had made similar comments on Iraq.
"Whatever the errors of the Iraqi authorities and their incorrect analysis of the situation, the Iraqi people must not be made to suffer for this," Saud had said on Tuesday.
Saud also said he gave Chirac a message from Saudi King Fahd. Neither he nor the Elysee presidential palace would comment on the contents.

Washington has been threatening further military action against Baghdad after missile strikes this month, accusing it of using its air defences to threaten Western surveillance flights in no-fly zones over northern and southern Iraq.

Chirac paid a two-day visit to Saudi Arabia in July, at which time he said close ties with Riyadh were key to the relationship Paris seeks to develop with the Arab world and nations of the Middle East in general.
